what: Content-addressed, HMAC-signed rules-bundle wire format: canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators), bundle_version = SHA-256 of the unsigned body (clients skip re-download on string equality), HMAC-SHA256 signature covering body + version so stale-rules-under-fresh-version tampering breaks verification.
use: Strong pattern for shipping RaceLab's KB and chassis schema templates to offline-first mobile clients: content-addressed versioning gives free cache invalidation in expo-sqlite, and signing prevents tampered advice bundles. ~80 lines, trivially re-expressed in TS.
reasoning: Verified: bundle.py is an ~80-line, dependency-free Python module (only hashlib/hmac/json) implementing canonical JSON, content-addressed bundle_version (SHA-256 of the canonical unsigned body), and HMAC-SHA256 signing that covers bundle_version so stale-rules-under-fresh-version spoofing breaks verification — exactly as claimed, with the spoof case explicitly tested in tests/test_coaching_bundle.py (test_verify_bundle_raises_when_bundle_version_tampered). Not copypaste because it is Python, but it is a genuine scheme: RaceLab must ship chassis schema templates (and optionally KB subsets) to offline-first expo-sqlite clients, and content-addressing-as-version gives zero-bookkeeping cache invalidation while the version-covered-by-signature detail is a subtle design point teams typically miss. The serving endpoint adds an instructive posture (503 rather than serving unsigned when the secret is unconfigured; version=latest param reserved for future pinning).
adapt: Re-express in TypeScript inside packages/schema as a shared util used by both apps/api (sign) and apps/mobile (verify/cache): the critical porting trap is canonical JSON — JS JSON.stringify does NOT sort keys, so use an RFC 8785 (JCS) implementation or json-stable-stringify identically on both sides, or the client-recomputed hash will never match. Use node:crypto on the Next.js side and expo-crypto (SHA-256) on mobile; store bundle_version in expo-sqlite and send it as an ETag-style query/header so unchanged bundles return 304/skip-download. One real design correction for RaceLab: LAP verifies with a shared HMAC secret because its clients are trusted; a mobile app binary cannot hold a shared secret safely, so if on-device verification matters, swap HMAC for an Ed25519 signature (tweetnacl/expo-crypto) with the public key in the app — keep everything else (canonical bytes, content-addressed version, signature covering version + format_version) unchanged. Also copy the endpoint posture from coaching.py's get_rules_bundle: refuse to serve unsigned with a 503 when the signing key is unconfigured, and reserve a version param now to allow pinned-version retrieval later without a wire-format break; ignore the rest of coaching.py (insight flagging) — it is LAP-specific. The test file is included because it documents the exact tamper/spoof contract the TS port should reproduce.
